episodes.211792: Isolated thunderstorms move southeast across the eastern Colorado plains during the late afternoon and evening of May 9th. Wind gusts up to 70 mph accompanied the stronger thunderstorms.
episodes.211952: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across north central Oklahoma during the early afternoon of the 8th, along a cold front approaching the region from the northwest. The thunderstorms spread across eastern Oklahoma during the mid afternoon and evening. The atmosphere became moderately unstable during the afternoon ahead of the cold front in eastern Oklahoma, and deep-layer wind shear increased across the region with the approach of an upper level disturbance. The combination of moderately strong instability and strong deep-layer wind shear resulted in some thunderstorms evolving into supercell thunderstorms, the strongest of which produced large hail up to three inches in diameter and damaging wind.
episodes.211953: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across northeastern Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 8th, along a cold front approaching the region from the northwest. The thunderstorms spread into northwestern Arkansas during the evening. The atmosphere became moderately unstable during the afternoon ahead of the cold front in eastern Oklahoma and northwestern Arkansas, and deep-layer wind shear increased across the region with the approach of an upper level disturbance. The combination of moderately strong instability and strong deep-layer wind shear resulted in some thunderstorms evolving into supercell thunderstorms, the strongest of which produced large hail up to golf ball size.
episodes.212045: An isolated thunderstorm produced a tornado in Columbus County, NC.
episodes.212727: Several severe storms moved across the region, primarily following the Interstate 80 corridor through Wyoming and into western Nebraska.
episodes.212728: Several severe storms moved across the region, primarily following the Interstate 80 corridor through Wyoming and into western Nebraska.
episodes.212791: A stationary frontal boundary as well as both a Gulf of Mexico and Atlantic coast sea breeze combined with plentiful diurnal instability to produce robust thunderstorms across northeast FL during the afternoon and evening hours. Along with isolated severe thunderstorm activity, PWATs around 1.8 inches and slow moving/training convection resulted in very heavy rainfall and localized minor flooding.
episodes.213022: Over Mother's Day weekend, a slow-moving cold front triggered scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across North and Central Texas. The majority of these storms occurred on Mother's Day (May 10), with many reaching severe levels and large hail becoming the most frequent report. Hail up to 4.5 was reported in Hamilton County.
episodes.213252: A line of storms crossed over the Eastern Great Lakes and moved into the Niagara Frontier to Genesee Valley producing sporadic reports of damaging winds.
episodes.213259: A cluster of strong storms moved across the western coastal waters with measured gusts of 34 knots or greater.
episodes.213311: Warm, moist air combined with the influence of a dryline located across the eastern portion of the Texas Panhandle. This resulted in the development of an isolated thunderstorm during the evening of May 9th. With enough cold air present in the upper atmosphere, this allowed for large hail to grow within the storm and fall across portions of eastern Texas Panhandle. Additional storms developed during the early morning hours of May 10th along a southward moving cold front. These early morning storms produced hail between 1 and 1.5 over the northeastern combined Panhandles.
episodes.213364: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed along a cold front across portions of northern and central Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 8th, spreading southward into southern Oklahoma and western-north Texas through the evening. Large to very large hail was the main storm hazard with several supercell thunderstorms during this time. Sporadic wind damage was also observed, including on the southwest side of the Oklahoma City Metropolitan Area.
episodes.213365: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed along a cold front across portions of northern and central Oklahoma during the afternoon of the 8th, spreading southward into southern Oklahoma and western-north Texas through the evening. Large to very large hail was the main storm hazard with several supercell thunderstorms during this time.
episodes.213366: The passage of a southeastward-moving upper system (and associated surface front) fostered scattered severe thunderstorms during the evening of the 9th, focused across portions of western Oklahoma. Large to very large hail was the main storm hazard amid steep lapse rates and strong wind shear, sufficient for supercells. Focused areas of wind damage occurred near Sayre and northeast of Lawton as well.
episodes.213476: A thunderstorm over northern Oakland county produced 1 inch hail.
episodes.213523: Friday night into Saturday, May 8-9, 2026, strong to severe thunderstorms in association with atmospheric disturbances initially developed across Zapata County on the 8th, before redeveloping as a single severe thunderstorm that waxed and waned between Starr and Cameron County on May 9th. Large hail was initially reported in Starr County just after daybreak on the 9th, before the storm re-strengthened in Hidalgo and Cameron County by mid-morning. The episode culminated into a microburst that caused structural damage to roofs, traffic lights, fences, homes, trailers, and power poles as well as trees in central Cameron County. There were 3 injuries, two requiring hospitalization, where poorly constructed mobile-type homes were destroyed.||At least 45,000 customers were without power at peak or just after the storms crossed the populated IH-2 corridor from near McAllen to east of Harlingen, one of the more widespread outages in recent memory.
episodes.213578: A thunderstorm moving across the Detroit River produced a wind gust of 35 knots.
episodes.213821: Discrete thunderstorms in southeast Oklahoma congealed into a mesoscale convective complex as they moved southeast into northern Louisiana early morning of May 9th. The system consisted of clusters and linear segments moving rapidly eastward, while localized cell mergers and brief training occurred within the broader complex. The storms produced widespread damaging winds from the northshore of Lake Pontchartrain.
episodes.213822: Discrete thunderstorms in southeast Oklahoma congealed into a mesoscale convective complex as they moved southeast into northern Louisiana early morning of May 9th. The system consisted of clusters and linear segments moving rapidly eastward, while localized cell mergers and brief training occurred within the broader complex. The storms produced widespread damaging winds from storms over coastal Mississippi.
episodes.213823: Discrete thunderstorms in southeast Oklahoma congealed into a mesoscale convective complex as they moved southeast into northern Louisiana early morning of May 9th. The system consisted of clusters and linear segments moving rapidly eastward, while localized cell mergers and brief training occurred within the broader complex. The storms produced widespread severe wind gusts over local coastal waters.
episodes.213876: A weak surface frontal boundary became stationary across portions of Northeast Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon of May 8th, as a shortwave trough traversed southeast into Oklahoma. Diurnal heating within a moist air mass contributed to strong instability near the front, with the upper trough resulting in enhanced large scale forcing for the development of scattered severe thunderstorms during the evening and overnight hours across portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northern Louisiana. These storms produced multiple reports of large hail, with one isolated severe storm resulting in quarter size hail falling in the Emmet community in Nevada County Arkansas.
episodes.213877: A weak surface frontal boundary became stationary across portions of Northeast Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon of May 8th, as a shortwave trough traversed southeast into Oklahoma. Diurnal heating within a moist air mass contributed to strong instability near the front, with the upper trough resulting in enhanced large scale forcing for the development of scattered severe thunderstorms during the evening and overnight hours across portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northern Louisiana. Several reports of large hail were received across Northeast Texas before the storms weakened after 1 am on the morning of the 9th.
episodes.213881: A weak surface frontal boundary became stationary across portions of Northeast Texas and North Louisiana during the afternoon of May 8th, as a shortwave trough traversed southeast into Oklahoma. Diurnal heating within a moist air mass contributed to strong instability near the front, with the upper trough resulting in enhanced large scale forcing for the development of scattered severe thunderstorms during the evening and overnight hours across portions of Northeast Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and Northern Louisiana. Several reports of large hail were received across Northwest Louisiana before the storms weakened after 2 am on the morning of the 9th.
episodes.213909: A brief tornado formed out of the thunderstorm to north of Ten Sleep.
episodes.213955: Outflow boundaries from convection over North Texas provided enough lift to generate thunderstorms over South-Central Texas during the afternoon. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.213964: The 2026 spring breakup along the Yukon River was highly dynamic, defined by a combination of thermal ice decay and severe mechanical ice jams. Because of an exceptionally cold winter and a cool spring, the river ice was thicker than normal and had not deteriorated significantly before the main breakup front arrived. Early-season flooding was driven by localized snowmelt and ice jams on independent river systems and upper sections of the Yukon River.
episodes.214031: On the afternoon and evening of Saturday, May 9, 2026, a line of thunderstorms swept across Lake Erie, Northern Ohio, and Northwest Pennsylvania. Within this line, several severe thunderstorms produced marine wind gusts, wind gusts over land, and wind damage over land areas.
episodes.214039: On the afternoon and evening of Saturday, May 9, 2026, a line of thunderstorms swept across Lake Erie, several severe thunderstorms produced marine wind gusts.
episodes.214075: A cold front stalled across the region while multiple short waves moved overhead. This produce multiple days of unsettled weather.
episodes.214129: Lightning hit a fisherman that was standing under a pine tree.
episodes.214324: A thunderstorm produced gusty winds as it moved along the northern Brevard Coast.

An ice jam on the Koyukuk River near Hughes impounded a significant volume of water. This caused water levels to submerge properties in the lower sections of the community, directly impacting local residences, school property, and the airport. Local residents and members of the Alaska State EOC indicated that the ice set up late Friday night and then released Saturday afternoon. However, a secondary jam set up soon after which was responsible for sending most of the water into the community.  Numerous families were sheltered at the local community hall which is located on higher ground.

Just after 1000 AM CDT May 9, 2026, a strong microburst descended in central Cameron County from a small but potent line of thunderstorms and produced damage along a west-northwest to east-southeast oriented line starting from Harlingen, TX through Laureles, TX.  Overall damage was observed to traffic lights, several homes, powerlines, poles, fences, crops, and trees. At least a dozen homes had |various degrees of damage. The worst damage was to a poorly constructed |single wide type structure in Green Valley Farms, where two persons were injured, including an elderly woman who sought shelter underneath the structure and had broken ribs.  Another trailer-style residence on Country Boy Road, east of Green Valley Farms, had its roof ripped off, and debris fell onto a teenaged resident's head, requiring hospitalization.||At least five more recreational vehicles/mobile homes - with wheels and unanchored - were damaged. Hundreds of medium to large tree limbs were blown |down. Several signs including one billboard and two restaurant signs were blown down along the track. Power poles and lines were blown down in the same direction (west-northwest to east-southeast). The NWS Damage Survey reported an estimated path length of nearly 13 miles, and an average path width of 2 miles. Detailed notable wind damage reports from the damage survey were as follows:||*1011 AM CDT: Partial roof removal from a greenhouse at Lowe's, and a leaning power pole on the property (east Harlingen)...estimated wind 69 mph.|*1019 AM CDT: Old wooden billboard blown off its pole at intersection of US Highway 77 business and the frontage road. Wind speed estimated at 75 mph.  2.3 miles south-southeast of San Benito.|Wind speed estimated at approximately 75-80 feet AGL (24 meters)|*1021 AM CDT: Poorly constructed roof was ripped off and ended up collapsing, then part ended up behind the structure. Young resident (16 year old girl) was struck by falling debris and injured, requiring hospitalization.  4 miles east-southeast of downtown San Benito (just east of Green Valley Farms)...estimated wind 70 mph.|*1024 AM CDT: Poorly built and unanchored older single wide trailer style home blown away from location and demolished. In background, much of another single-wide was destroyed after roof was ripped off. Eighteen persons were in the structures; two were injured. One elderly woman had broken ribs after sheltering under the home; another had unknown lesser injuries. Several had minor cuts and bruises. Poor construction and full exposure to the wind, commensurate with nearby damage, suggested 75-80 mph wind in Green Valley Farms (4 miles east-southeast of San Benito)|*1025 AM CDT:  Very poorly affixed roof was partially ripped off a single-wide, with rusted sheet metal. Wind speed estimated to be close to 70-75 mph per nearby damage (4.5 miles east-southeast of San Benito).|*1026 AM CDT:  A dozen wooden telephone poles snapped, likely due to a domino effect. Medium to large limbs of every tree at residence near intersection of Adams and San Jose Road were damaged. Speed here was likely 80 mph (among highest of surveyed area). 4.4 miles east of San Benito. |*1030 AM CDT:  Uprooted large and old tree, snapped near the base (uprooted). Many other large limbs down in the neighborhood in west Laureles. Estimated wind speed was 80 mph.|*1033 AM CDT: Damage to mobile home/RV, downed powerlines, and damage to nearby trees on east side of Laureles.  Wind speed estimated at 75 mph at this location.||Final damages are unknown, but based on survey results, $500,000 is a fair assessment as of this writing.
